label: copy-phase x fed back as input, early in recall and near the end of the sequence
explanation: Token-specific feature: fires only when the input is x during the copy phase (the model re-reading its own copied x). 99.98% of activations land on copy-phase x inputs, with zero activity in the original or delimiter phases and essentially none on other tokens. Among copy-phase x inputs it fires on only about 30%, gated by position: mostly recall_idx 2-3 (89% of mass), less at 1 and 4, never at 0 or >=5, and favoring short sequences (L 4-5) with few outputs left (to_go <= 3). The strongest activations are short sequences (L=4) where x is original token 1, e.g. y x j 2 <DEL> y [x]. It is weaker (lowest quartile) for x deep in long sequences, and repeated x (in_count >= 2) is weaker too. It does not fire on x in the original phase. Predicate: dev F1 0.77, mass recall 0.88. Precision is limited because the positional gating is graded, not a sharp cutoff.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: x, g, n, -, r, k; least: 2, o, u, <DEL>) and the next token to output (most: 2, b, u, j, g, 0; least: n, 1, -, x); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=2, L=3 & t=4.
